headline: A rough day on the ASX — PLS and GXAI lead the falls — while MSFT surged 5.7% last night on strong AI momentum, and the RBA held rates steady giving mortgage holders some breathing room.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped 5.7% last night in a big single-session move. No specific news catalyst in the data, but MSFT has been riding strong AI tailwinds — the market is increasingly rewarding its deep integration of AI tools across its product suite. Earnings are on the horizon too, which may be bringing buyers in early.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara dropped 6.3% at today's close — a nasty session. Lithium stocks globally remain under pressure as oversupply concerns weigh on the sector. Similar lithium stocks like Sigma Lithium (SGML) also slid on the same day despite broader market gains, suggesting it's a sector-wide issue rather than anything Pilbara-specific.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF fell 5% today, which is a significant daily move. GOOG (a big holding inside this ETF) dropped 2.2% last night, and broader AI-themed stocks came under pressure. The pullback likely reflects some profit-taking after a strong run in AI-related names.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 2.2% last night — no major company-specific news was flagged, but it underperformed the broader NASDAQ. The market appears to be favouring Microsoft's AI narrative right now, which can pull money out of GOOG in the short term.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets had a soft day, with VGE falling 2.4% at today's close. The ETF tracks countries like China, India and Brazil, and sentiment around these markets has been choppy. Oil falling 3.7% overnight may have weighed on energy-heavy emerging market economies.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS tracks the entire US sharemarket and dipped 1.5% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's mild softness in the NASDAQ (-0.24%) and S&P 500 (-0.05%). A fairly unremarkable session — no single big catalyst.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG slipped about 0.6% today — a small move for this broadly diversified fund. It holds Australian and global shares across growth assets, so it absorbed some of the weakness in both local and US markets, cushioned by its diversification.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL bucked the trend with a small 0.9% gain today on the ASX — a bit surprising given oil (WTI crude) dropped sharply by 3.7% last night. The ASX close likely hadn't fully priced in that overnight oil fall yet, so watch for potential drag on FUEL on Monday.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two was basically flat last night, down just 0.08%. GTA VI pre-orders opened this week and initial market reaction has been mixed — the digital-only format and pricing details disappointed some investors earlier in the week, though the stock has largely stabilised since.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Pilbara Minerals down 6.3% — hold but watch closely
watch_today.detail: Pilbara has now shed over 25% against your cost base. Today's 6.3% drop is part of a broader lithium sector selloff — oversupply concerns aren't going away quickly. There's no immediate recovery catalyst visible. Unless you have conviction on a lithium price rebound, it's worth deciding whether you want to average down or trim. For now, hold and monitor.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF drops 5% today — hold and don't panic
watch_today.detail: A 5% single-day fall looks scary but this ETF is volatile by nature — it's concentrated in high-growth AI names. GOOG, one of its bigger holdings, fell last night too. The AI story is still intact long-term; this looks more like a sector rotation day than a fundamental breakdown. Sit tight unless the whole AI theme starts unwinding.

watch_today.title: MSFT surged 5.7% last night — strong hold, consider adding
watch_today.detail: Microsoft had a standout session last night, jumping nearly 6%. It's still down about 15.8% against your total invested amount, so the stock has room to recover. With earnings coming up and AI momentum firmly behind it, this is looking like a genuine recovery play. Worth watching for an entry point if you're considering topping up.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil fell 3.7% last night — brace for a drag on Monday
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) dropped from $71.92 to $69.23 last night as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a key oil route in the Middle East — rebounded, easing supply fears. FUEL.AX actually rose 0.9% today because the ASX hadn't fully caught up with that oil drop yet. Monday could see FUEL give back some of today's gain. Nothing to act on today, but keep it on the radar.

watch_today.title: RBA holds interest rates — good news for the economy and your ETFs
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank left rates on hold, giving mortgage holders relief and keeping consumer confidence supported. Lower rate pressure is generally good for growth assets like VDHG and VTS. No action needed, but it's a positive backdrop for your diversified holdings.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-order reaction settling down — hold
watch_today.detail: GTA VI pre-orders opened this week but the market's initial reaction was a sell — the digital-only format and pricing details disappointed some. The stock has largely stabilised now, down just 0.08% last night. You're up about 4% overall on TTWO. No reason to sell, but the real test will be closer to the actual launch.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 edged up 0.18% today to close at 8,764 — a quiet, slightly positive session for the local market overall, though several individual holdings had rough days. Last night in the US, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ were broadly flat (S&P -0.05%, NASDAQ -0.24%) — not a big mover either way. The standout market story was oil, which dropped 3.7% as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz — a major oil supply route — recovered, reducing fears about supply disruptions. Gold continued its climb, up 1.2% to hit $4,079 USD per ounce, suggesting some investors are still seeking safety. The Aussie dollar barely moved, sitting at US$0.69.

indicators.note: Slight gain today — broader market held up despite weakness in individual names

indicators.note: Dropped sharply as Strait of Hormuz shipping normalised, easing supply fears

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Keeps climbing — investors still buying safety

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Barely moved — steady as she goes

politics.summary: Two big domestic stories broke this week: the RBA left interest rates on hold (good news for borrowers), and the Labor government's tax reform package passed into law. Both have real implications for everyday Australians and for markets.

stories.title: RBA leaves interest rates on hold — relief for mortgage holders
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia decided to leave its cash rate (the interest rate it sets that flows through to home loans) on hold at its latest meeting. For anyone with a mortgage, this means no new increase in monthly repayments — welcome news after a long run of hikes. It also signals the RBA thinks inflation is under enough control that it doesn't need to tighten further right now. Positive backdrop for consumer spending and growth-oriented investments like VDHG.

stories.title: Labor's tax reform package passes into law
stories.why_it_matters: The Labor government's tax reform legislation has officially become law after passing parliament. The article text wasn't available, but based on what's been publicly debated, this package is a significant political win for the government. The reforms have been contentious — watch for more detail on what this means for property investors and high-income earners as the specifics are reported in coming days.

ai.summary: The big AI story this week is the US government tightening its grip on which companies can access the most powerful new AI models — with OpenAI limiting access to 'trusted partners' only, and Anthropic's new Mythos model being released under similar controlled conditions. AI regulation is also heating up globally.

stories.title: OpenAI limits new AI models to 'trusted partners' at request of US government
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has asked OpenAI to restrict access to its most advanced new AI models, limiting them to a small group of 'trusted partners' rather than making them publicly available. This is a significant shift — it means the most powerful AI tools are now being treated almost like sensitive technology, controlled by the government. For investors, it signals regulators are getting serious about who can use frontier AI, which could slow commercial rollout of cutting-edge models but also creates a moat for the companies that get approved access.

stories.title: Trump admin allows Anthropic to release Mythos AI model to select companies and government agencies
stories.why_it_matters: In the same vein, the Trump administration has given Anthropic (the company behind the Claude AI assistant) the green light to release its new 'Mythos' model — but only to a curated list of companies and government agencies, not the general public. This is the first time a major AI model has been launched under explicit government supervision in this way. It sets a precedent: future powerful AI tools may all go through a government approval process before broad release, similar to how defence technology is handled.

stories.title: Spain introduces new Organic Law on AI governance — key points
stories.why_it_matters: Spain has passed a major new law specifically governing how AI can be used — one of the first countries in the world to do so with dedicated national legislation (separate from the EU's broader AI Act). The law covers things like transparency requirements, accountability for AI systems used in public services, and restrictions on high-risk applications. It's part of a global wave of AI regulation that's building fast — relevant context for anyone holding AI-exposed stocks like GXAI.AX, as more regulation generally means higher compliance costs for AI companies.

stories.title: Australia warned about 'AI cowboys' amid data centre building frenzy
stories.why_it_matters: A warning has been raised in Australia about unregulated AI operators — dubbed 'AI cowboys' — rushing to build data centres and deploy AI without proper oversight, governance, or safety checks. The concern is that the race to build AI infrastructure is moving faster than the rules designed to keep it safe and accountable. For Australian investors, it highlights that local AI regulation is still catching up, and that not all AI investment will be in quality, well-governed operators.

sport.summary: Big NRL Round 17 weekend underway — the Dolphins won a tight one at home, the Roosters edged the Broncos (Brisbane's seventh straight loss), and the Bulldogs thrashed the Titans. Wimbledon has kicked off with some big storylines, including an Aussie wildcard qualifier and a wide-open women's draw. The NRL is also reportedly closing in on a mammoth $5 billion broadcast deal.

stories.title: Dolphins pip Warriors 26-24 in thriller, but superstar picks up injury scare
stories.why_it_matters: Your local team the Dolphins won a nail-biter at Suncorp Stadium today, 26-24 over the Warriors. Good result for the Dolphins who are pushing for a finals spot — but the win was overshadowed by a reported injury to one of their stars during the match. The club is reportedly 'rattled' by the news. Full extent of the injury should be clearer after the weekend.

stories.title: Roosters edge Broncos 24-18 — Brisbane's seventh straight loss
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters defeated the Brisbane Broncos 24-18 at Suncorp Stadium on Friday night, handing Brisbane their seventh loss in a row. The Broncos coach has rejected suggestions the season is done, but the pressure is mounting. The NRL has also weighed in on the form of three State of Origin players from the Broncos squad following the continued poor run. The Bulldogs also beat the Titans 30-12, with Nick Crichton impressing in a new role, keeping Canterbury's finals hopes alive.

stories.title: NRL on the verge of signing historic $5 billion broadcast deal
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL is reportedly close to finalising a new broadcast rights deal worth around $5 billion — which would be the biggest in the game's history. A deal of this size would massively boost club revenues and player payments for the next broadcast cycle. No specific broadcasters named yet in the reports, but it's a significant signal that the NRL's commercial value is at an all-time high.

stories.title: Wimbledon: Aussie young gun dealt tough draw, women's field wide open
stories.why_it_matters: Wimbledon 2026 is underway and an Australian young gun has qualified through to the main draw — only to be handed a brutal first-round match described as a 'Serena shock' draw. Separately, an Australian qualifier named Sweeny battled through to the main draw showing plenty of fight. The women's draw is being described as unusually wide open this year, with no clear favourite — making for potentially exciting viewing across the fortnight.
